Commentary.Commentary: Right then, Afghanistan have just pulled off a Trans-Tasmanian double in this World Cup and just like the Kiwis, they might have just sent the Aussies packing as well but there's still a lot of cricket to be played. Next up is a Group 2 clash in the Super Eight stage with the USA taking on England at the Kensington Oval, Bridgetown, Barbados on Sunday, 23 June. That game will begin at 8 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT) but you can join us a lot sooner for the build-up. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Rashid Khan, the victorious skipper of Afghanistan says that it is a massive win for them. Adds that they came close in the previous two World Cups, and it feels great to finally get the better of the Aussies. Tells that he is very happy with the performance of his team, and they learned from their mistakes which helped them a lot. Mentions that they knew 140 was going to be a good score but they could not finish as they hoped. Says that the opening partnership was important as the wicket became difficult towards the end. Further adds that it is the beauty of this team as they have a lot of all-rounders who can chip in, and Gulbadin Naib stepped up in this game, and Nabi also picked up a crucial wicket early on. Ends by saying that this is a big victory for them, and now they will focus on the next match as they have all the chances to make it to the semis.

Mitchell Marsh, the captain of Australia says that the opposition got 20 runs too many and they played a really good game of cricket. Adds that a lot of teams have bowled first throughout the tournament and they were happy to bowl first. Mentions that it was an off night for them in the field and they have to own it. Adds that they knew what to expect coming into this game and they were outplayed by Afghanistan. On their clash against India, he says that he is looking forward to it and they just need to win and will be focused on it.

Gulbadin Naib is the Player of the Match for his match-winning spell with the ball. He says they have waited a long time for this and it is a great moment for the team and the entire nation. Adds that the wicket was not easy to bat and they took a few things from the first innings which worked for them. Tells that he is happy that Rashid Khan trusted him and says that it was a complete team performance and everyone played their part. Mentions that they have played some good cricket in this World Cup as they beat New Zealand in the group stages and now they have finally beaten Australia which is a great achievement for their cricket. Further adds that they can now rest and then focus on the next game against Bangladesh.
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Mitchell Marsh won the toss and opted to bowl first on a pitch where most people thought that batting first was the way to go. It was a gritty effort from the Afghanistan openers as they put on a 100-plus stand to set things up for their side. Both Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran reached their fifties but got out soon after and the middle order just wasn't able to kick on from the get-go. Adam Zampa was yet again very consistent for Australia and Pat Cummins made history by picking up hat-tricks in consecutive World Cup matches. Mohammad Nabi managed to drag Afghanistan close to the 150-run mark with a boundary off the final delivery and that gave them a bit of impetus. In reply, Australia's top order misfired and they were left chasing the game and eventually, they ran out of steam.

This will be a very tough pill to swallow for Australia and they will have to regroup quickly as they face a world-class Indian side next in a do-or-die clash to make it to the semifinals. Having bowled first, they knew it was going to be tough at the start and towards the backend to hit the ball cleanly but they couldn't manage to keep wickets in hand to take full advantage of those middle overs. Travis Head went for a duck and David Warner looked tentative, the skipper Mitchell Marsh did counter-attack but he too fell and left them in a hole. It was Glenn Maxwell who really dug them out of trouble and all signs indicated that there would be a repeat of that unforgettable match from last year's ODI World Cup but a stellar catch from Noor Ahmad meant that Maxwell got out on 59 and couldn't stay on till the end. There wasn't much to write about the rest of the batting and they were quite well beaten in the end.

Afghanistan had a defendable total on the board given the nature of the surface and they started off brilliantly with the ball. The move to give Naveen-ul-Haq the first over instead of Fazalhaq Farooqi was spot on as Naveen cleaned up Travis Head and from there on, the Afghans were able to attack. They had Australia reeling at 32/3 before things started to fall apart and the spinners didn't do much damage in the middle phase. It was a sensational spell from Gulbadin Naib in the second half of the innings that really turned the tide and he picked up four wickets to get into the tailenders and Naveen came back in to pick up three wickets in total. Azmatullah Omarzai rounded off a fine display as he got the final wicket and Afghanistan bundled out Australia and picked up their first-ever win against them in T20Is.

AFGHANISTAN ARE ALIVE AND KICKING! Group 1 of the Super Eight stage has just been blown wide open as Afghanistan notch up their most famous win ever and they have dealt a hefty blow to the reigning ODI World Champions in their bid to hold the Test, ODI and T20I World Championships all at the same time. The Afghans came close last year in the ODI World Cup and let it slip through their hands but this time, they have got things perfect and the players are on the field in utter jubilation and rightly so too.

AFGHANISTAN WIN BY 21 RUNS!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it through! Tossed up, full and on off, Glenn Maxwell goes down, almost loses his balance but still manages to execute the reverse sweep towards the third man fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Nangeyalia Kharote to Glenn Maxwell, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on middle, Marcus Stoinis drills it down to long off for another run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Nangeyalia Kharote to Marcus Stoinis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes short and on middle, Glenn Maxwell watches it through and steers it towards point for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Nangeyalia Kharote to Glenn Maxwell, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nangeyalia Kharote begins with a flatter delivery, full and on leg, Marcus Stoinis tucks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Nangeyalia Kharote to Marcus Stoinis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nangeyalia Kharote to have a bowl now.
Darts this one full and on leg, Glenn Maxwell misses his flick and gets hit on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Mohammad Nabi to Glenn Maxwell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter, short and on off, turns in, Glenn Maxwell winds up for the big shot but ends up patting it to short covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Mohammad Nabi to Glenn Maxwell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted, full and on middle, Marcus Stoinis goes down and sweeps it towards deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Mohammad Nabi to Marcus Stoinis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit short and on middle, Marcus Stoinis clips it towards square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mohammad Nabi to Marcus Stoinis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, full and on middle, Marcus Stoinis knocks it towards the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Mohammad Nabi to Marcus Stoinis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Marcus Stoinis walks out to the middle now.

OUT! TAKEN! 'The President gets rid of the Bull here'! A massive wicket for Afghanistan and they are on top here. Mohammad Nabi starts with a floated delivery, full and around middle, David Warner goes down to sweep it away, but only manages to get a top edge behind towards short fine leg where Noor Ahmad settles under it and pouches it safely. In-form Wanrer goes and Australia are in big trouble!
Commentary.Howout: c Noor Ahmad b Mohammad Nabi
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mohammad Nabi to David Warner, OUT! c Noor Ahmad b Mohammad Nabi.

Commentary.Commentary: Doing a bit too much! Just short of a good length and over off stump, this one jags back in sharply and Glenn Maxwell is beaten past the inside edge. The ball hits the pads and rolls to short third.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Azmatullah Omarzai to Glenn Maxwell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length in the channel outside off stump, Glenn Maxwell plays it away to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Azmatullah Omarzai to Glenn Maxwell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Limited footwork but the hand skills on display were immaculate. Pitched up around middle, Glenn Maxwell just gets inside the line and flicks it nonchalantly over the mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Azmatullah Omarzai to Glenn Maxwell, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length and around off stump, Glenn Maxwell jams the ball down into the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Azmatullah Omarzai to Glenn Maxwell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Too straight from Azmat and that's easy pickings for Glenn Maxwell. Good length but angled into the pads, Maxwell tickles it past the diving keeper and the ball rolls away into the fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Glenn Maxwell, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: That one stayed down quite a bit! Azmatullah Omarzai begins from around the stumps and bowls it a bit fuller and in the channel around off, getting it to nip away. David Warner looks to play but the low bounce beats the inside edge and the keeper gets a bad bounce as well. They pick up a bye as the ball rolls to short third.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Azmatullah Omarzai to David Warner, Bye.

Commentary.Commentary: This is bowled quite full and around off stump, Glenn Maxwell stays back in the crease and works it away well wide of mid on for a couple of quick runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Glenn Maxwell, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches this one up wide of the off stump and gets it to angle across, Glenn Maxwell reaches out and has a waft at it but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Glenn Maxwell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! That in-between length now in and around the off stump and just going on with the angle, Glenn Maxwell ends up playing inside the line of the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Glenn Maxwell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another slower one, floated up quite full and angling back onto the base of the off stump, David Warner plays it late and angles it away towards backward point for another single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Fazalhaq Farooqi to David Warner, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and outside off, slanting it across the right-hander, Glenn Maxwell reaches out and slices the ball away to deep third for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Glenn Maxwell, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off from Farooqi as well and this is pitched up on the fifth stump line, David Warner lets the ball come on and guides it past backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Fazalhaq Farooqi to David Warner, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off again and bowled fuller outside off stump, Glenn Maxwell looks to cover drive but fails to get it away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Naveen-ul-Haq to Glenn Maxwell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit fuller and angling in from middle and leg, David Warner gets inside the line and flicks it nicely down to fine leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Naveen-ul-Haq to David Warner, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling down leg! Naveen-ul-Haq goes wider on the crease and angles in a fuller delivery into the pads, Glenn Maxwell walks across to flick but misses and the ball goes off the pads in front of square leg. They get a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Naveen-ul-Haq to Glenn Maxwell, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will walk out now?

OUT! CAUGHT! Excellent change of pace from Naveen-ul-Haq and Mitchell Marsh has to walk back after a promising start. Smart cricket from Naveen as he knows Marsh is eager to get on the front foot and drive and Naveen takes pace off, bowling it fuller and around off stump. Marsh goes through with the shot and ends up lifting it high but only towards mid on. Mohammad Nabi there settles under it and snaffles it with the reverse cup.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Naveen-ul-Haq to Mitchell Marsh, OUT! c Mohammad Nabi b Naveen-ul-Haq.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length, outside off and played off the front foot straight towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Naveen-ul-Haq to Mitchell Marsh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! This is good counter-attacking cricket from Mitchell Marsh here. Full and wide of the off stump, looking to angle it back in, Marsh gets on the front foot and gets to the pitch of the ball before lifting it away square over covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Naveen-ul-Haq to Mitchell Marsh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length around the top of off stump, David Warner gets on the front foot and eases it towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Fazalhaq Farooqi to David Warner, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Well, that was an outrageous attempted shot. On a good length outside off and swinging away, David Warner sits down on one knee and looks to fetch and slog it over mid-wicket but is well beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Fazalhaq Farooqi to David Warner, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller in length again and swinging back in from middle, Mitchell Marsh heaves it off the inner half of the bat to mid on and scampers through for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Top shot! Pitched up in and around the off stump, Mitchell Marsh plants his front foot ahead and hammers it on the up and well to the right of mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Mitchell Marsh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that swung in late and Mitchell Marsh was almost too late on it as well. Nice and full, swinging back in from middle, Marsh manages to get the front leg out of the way and heaves it away in front of deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Mitchell Marsh, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES! A bit too straight to begin with from Fazalhaq Farooqi and those are free runs for Australia. Pitched up on the pads and swinging back in, Mitchell Marsh misses the flick and the ball goes off the pads and rolls away into the fine leg fence for four leg byes.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Mitchell Marsh, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Fazalhaq Farooqi to share the attack.

Play and a miss, some start to the chase, Australia are 1 for 1 after 1. Back to around the stumps, pushed a bit fuller and wider, getting it to nibble away. David Warner comes forward to hit it through the off side but is beaten past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Naveen-ul-Haq to David Warner, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length around off stump and angling in, Mitchell Marsh tucks it neatly off his legs and past square leg to get the Aussie run chase going with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Naveen-ul-Haq to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit of a prolonged appeal for LBW but the umpire says no. Switches to over the wicket for the right-hander and angles it back in a quite fair bit on a good length and into the pads. Mitchell Marsh looks to pick it up over square leg but misses and gets hit high on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Naveen-ul-Haq to Mitchell Marsh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mitchell Marsh walks out to bat number 3,

OUT! BOWLED'EM! That is fantastic bowling and fantastic captaincy to give the first over to Naveen-ul-Haq instead of Fazalhaq Farooqi. Naveen stays around the stumps and bowls it quite full on the leg peg, angling in and gets that magical outswinger going. Travis Head hangs back, clears his leg and looks to smash this across the line but plays all around it and he hears the death rattle behind him. What an electrifying start from Afghanistan!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Naveen-ul-Haq to Travis Head, OUT! b Naveen-ul-Haq.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches this one up around the off stump line, Travis Head gets on the front foot and solidly strokes it away to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Naveen-ul-Haq to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: What a stinging delivery to start the chase! Naveen-ul-Haq comes from around the stumps and angles it in from outside off stump on a hard length. The ball nips away sharply and takes off after pitching leaving Travis Head quite perplexed.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Naveen-ul-Haq to Travis Head, No run.
